thread.title_full: MIT calculator shows rising cost of living for Ashe households - NewsBreak

author: Jesse Campbell
title: MIT calculator shows rising cost of living for Ashe households - NewsBreak
text:
By Jesse Campbell ,
14 hours ago
ASHE COUNTY — Both parents in a local two-child household would need to make at least $21.90 to afford basic necessities, according to the updated MIT Living Wage Calculator.
Massachusetts Institute of Technology developed the calculator and cross-referenced metric to inform local communities about local wage rates for full-time employees, according to mit.edu. It figures pricing for childcare, housing, food, transportation, medical expenses, and other monthly expenses.
The wage table for each county in the United States provides navigable data sets on hourly rates and compares poverty and minimum wages across demographics.
A working parent in a two-person, two-child household would need to earn at least $34.54 per hour, before taxes, to adequately cover expenses, while the poverty wage for this demographic is $15.87 an hour, according to the wage calculator.
However, federal poverty wage thresholds are not estimated survival wages. The minimum wage in North Carolina is $7.25 an hour.
The living wage for a two-person household with one working adult and no children is $26.29 an hour. The poverty wage for this demographic is $10.40 an hour.
Necessary wages increase for a one-person working household with children. One working adult in a two-person household, with one child, needs $32.17 per hour, according to the data. The poverty wage for a two-person household with one working adult and one to three children is $13.13, $15.87, and $18.60 per hour, per child, respectively.
Moreover, the data set reveals that a single person without children needs $18.89 an hour, before taxes, to cover basic expenses. A single parent raising one child alone needs $31.66 per hour. However, the sole wage earner would need to earn $46.49 per hour, before taxes, to care for three children properly.
Poverty wages for a single working parent in a one-, two-, or three-child household are $10.40, $13.13, and $15.87 per hour, per child, respectively, according to MIT data.
Click to livingwage.mit.edu/counties/ for more information.
